newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian town opposes nuclear waste processing plant.
newsitem.headline: Russian town opposes nuclear waste processing plant.

text.p: Residents of a small town on Russia's Pacific coast have voted against allowing a floating nuclear waste processing plant to be docked near them, officials said on Friday.

An official in Bolshoi Kamen 100 km (60 miles) north of the regional capital Vladivostok said 94 percent of participants in a non-binding poll held on Wednesday did not want the plant established anywhere nearby.
The official said 13,000 people of Bolshoi Kamen, or 44 percent of elegible voters, took part in the poll.
The floating plant, due to arrive in Bolshoi Kamen in early July, is intended to solve the problem of neutralising liquid waste left over after the dismantling of old Russian nuclear submarines.
The waste is now kept at two floating storage tanks outside docks where the submarines are decommissioned.
Regional governor Yevgeny Nazdratenko has warned that unless the problem of processing the waste is solved it will be dumped into the Sea of Japan, a threat which has triggered alarm in Tokyo.
